_about: Second fact check of 20 Oct 2026, at launch: the 58 facts newly scheduled for 20 Oct-25 Nov 2026 when Reckon 1 moved from 26 Oct to 20 Oct. Search only (titles, no snippets) plus the checkers own knowledge. Applied with tools/apply-ballpark-fixes.js; exclusions are in EXCLUDE in tools/build-reckon-batch.js.

places:85.n: There were once nearly 60. It still has more than any other city north of the Alps.

earth:68.q: How tall is the Old Man of Hoy, one of Britain’s tallest sea stacks, in metres?

space:72.q: How many hours does sunlight take to reach Pluto, on average?

animals:35.q: How many feathers does a tundra swan have?

build:69.q: How long are the Elizabeth line’s new tunnels under London in total, counting both bores, in kilometres?

excludeFromReckon.food:74: oldest edible honey: 3,000 years (Egyptian tombs, an unverified tale) and 5,500 years (Georgian tomb find, 2003) are both quoted, and neither was verified as edible
excludeFromReckon.food:17: UK tea per day: 100 million and 165 million cups are both quoted by the UK tea industry
excludeFromReckon.food:76: UK chocolate per person: about 8, 10 and 11 kg a year are all quoted, depending on year and survey definition
